Review of my experience getting a dental scaling treatment from someone with receding gums who was afraid of scaling because of the sensitivity that might be more severe than others. I had to change clinics every year because I hadn't found one that met my needs.

I saw this clinic because it's near my house and I drive past it regularly. The place is beautiful, like a cafe. I thought the service must be very expensive. I searched on Google and found only good customer reviews, so I decided to try it.

On the day of my dental scaling appointment, this was the first place that came to mind. I was impressed from the moment I messaged them; their responses reduced my anxiety and made me feel welcome.

My next impression was the service and the respect they showed. No matter how shabbily I was dressed, everyone at the clinic smiled and provided excellent service.

Dr. Ae was very kind and understood my concerns. I requested local anesthesia because of a bad experience before. Dr. Ae only injected anesthetic into my lower teeth where gums were severely receding, showing how gentle and patient she is. She carefully inserted the needle and administered the anesthetic; I didn't feel any pain. Even when scaling my upper teeth, which weren't anesthetized, I didn't experience any sensitivity, whereas before I would repeatedly stop the doctor because I couldn't bear the pain.

Dr. Ae's assistant was also very attentive. I didn't choke on the water at all. (I always choke when I get teeth cleaned elsewhere.) The doctor was polite, kind, and patient.

The doctor said he's a dental implant surgeon and doesn't do scaling anywhere else; he only does it for clients at his own clinic. He also wanted to create a clinic for people who are afraid of dental procedures. I feel very lucky to have met him; it erased my negative memories from previous teeth cleaning experiences.

As for the price, which I was worried about being unaffordable, it's the normal price for a private clinic, and I can use my social security insurance.

In short, I was very impressed. I've found a clinic that perfectly meets my needs.

The first thing that impressed me was how lovely the staff and dentist were; they spoke so politely. The place was relaxing, like a cafe.
The main point was that the dental check-up revealed I had four wisdom teeth, two above and two below. The dentist recommended removing them two at a time, which meant one would be extracted and the other would be surgically removed. I was terrified because I'd heard from people who had had them removed elsewhere that even just one tooth would cause excruciating pain and make it impossible to eat. They recommended removing them one at a time because removing both at once would be incredibly painful. But I decided to have both removed at once. On the day of the procedure, I was excited, scared, and couldn't sleep. First, the anesthetic injection was painless; I didn't feel anything at all. Pain score: 0/10. The dentist had a very light touch. I only felt something when they were probably prying or extracting the tooth with the instruments. But the doctor always tells you when you might feel pain or not, so don't worry. After the procedure, I bit on the gauze for 2 hours and felt a throbbing sensation, starting to feel like it might hurt. Once the gauze was removed, I took just one paracetamol tablet and slept. When I woke up, I didn't feel any pain at all! I ate soft foods for about a day, then ate normally until the stitches were removed, and I didn't feel any pain at all. My cheek was slightly swollen, but you wouldn't notice it unless you looked closely. For anyone who is afraid of wisdom tooth extraction or afraid of needles like me, I highly recommend coming here. It's great! ✨🫶🏻
